answer: Under fingerprint-cohort convex toll, every identity entering the reef network presents a TPM-attested device key, and its admission fee equals c·((n+1)²−n²), where n counts prior identities already enrolled with that same key. An ivory honest agent holding a unique key always pays exactly c, since n=0, while a sable farm reusing one key to mint m fakes pays c·(1+3+5+…+(2m−1)) = c·m² in total: 100 fakes cost 10,000c versus 100c for 100 honest solo-key agents, a 100× nonlinear penalty. Hardware attestation makes fresh keys costly, so mass attackers subsidize honest participants instead.
